description: FS-GG typed coordination engine — the schedulability model behind `fsgg-coord` as one total function over a board-state snapshot, plus the typed IO layer that drives it. It IS the coordination tool (ADR-0034/ADR-0040): the `fsgg-coord` shim resolves and execs it; there is no bash left to shadow.
releaseNotes:
0.19.0 — MINOR on the 0.x line, the repository's signal for caller-observable change.

This release carries sixteen engine commits after 0.18.0. The highest-weight change is the
wire-surface review-policy expansion (#2086/#2136): the engine now validates durable runtime-route
evidence and bounded independent-review/repair-phase marker vocabulary that receiver guidance
already requires. Patch is not defensible: callers receive new authoritative scheduling outcomes,
diagnostics, enforcement, and review/refusal contracts.

BLOCKED-WORK CORRECTNESS (#2079/#2098/#1933): a pending Blocked-by clear is authoritative within a
batch; a Blocked park is bound to its actual blocker; non-holder board writes preserve ordering; and
the typed protocol now states that Blocked by is a board field rather than issue-body prose. The last
change is emitted into worker guidance, so this package is the engine that makes that guidance true.

SAFE COMMAND CONTRACTS (#2110): verify-paths rejects a closing keyword that uses the board's
<repo>#<n> shorthand, because GitHub will not close an issue through that spelling.

PLANNING DIAGNOSTICS (#2117): batch stderr reports active items, wave capacity, open slots, and a
WAVE SHORTFALL without changing its machine-readable stdout.

SCHEDULING AND LIFECYCLE CONTRACTS (#2119/#2140/#2154/#2174): newline-separated Paths tokens survive
the wire; driver transitions are deterministic; generated operational facts expose review-policy and
delivery-receipt keys; and the engine now supplies the typed claim-to-done lifecycle used for guarded
landing, obligation receipts, completion, and cleanup.

EXTERNAL-OWNER AND RECONCILIATION CORRECTNESS (#2147/#2163/#2171/#2172): board reads and writes retain
the explicit external repository owner, take preserves it, and reconcile verifies its repairs from a
fresh projection while failing closed on malformed pagination.

Release-window commits: 445dcd9, 1c16276, df57b7b, 276e83c, 4a5bc86, 77e463f, aeb11d0, a7d9bac,
baa9ce9, a75b5ef, ef7bd37, 12aed34, 66ef539, 72dfc58, 15d978c, and 45b93a1.

PREVIOUS RELEASE NOTES (0.18.0):

Runtime changes merged after 0.17.0 make the packaged engine match the coordination and product-board
guidance already carried by Kit 0.24.0 and the driver manifest.

REPOSITORY-SCOPED TOUCH SETS (#2011): path declarations are interpreted in their declared Repo Scope,
so identical relative paths in different repositories no longer contend accidentally.

BOARD FACTS AND DIAGNOSTICS (#2040/#2042): scheduler facts are extracted behind a typed application
boundary, overlap refusals name the reserving holder, and board drivers receive structured rate-limit
classes instead of parsing prose (#2041).

SAFE RECONCILIATION (#1984/#2000/#2037): blocker-cleared repairs fail closed when the live PR probe
cannot be read, lint covers blocked verdicts, and deliberate human parks are distinguished from stale
blockers.

COMMAND AND SCHEDULER CORRECTIONS (#1991/#1992/#1993/#2031): option ownership and rendered flag
spellings agree with the command contract, dead scan rendering is removed, and filing a single-item
parallel lane is diagnosed rather than silently presented as fan-out.

Patch is not defensible: the 0.x tool gains result vocabulary, repository-scoped scheduling semantics,
and caller-visible refusal/diagnostic behavior.

PREVIOUS RELEASE NOTES (0.17.0):

TWO merged engine commits since 0.16.0.

REFUSAL SPELLINGS (#1573): refusal text is now derived from the command-contract flag spelling table,
including the non-long `-n` limit spelling. Contract output and a refusal can no longer silently name
different flags.

SAFE ROTATED-SESSION RECOVERY (#1857): a live claim carrying this worker id but a different session
still refuses — the #419 twin guard is not weakened — but its diagnostic now names the marker session
and the `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`/`FSGG_WORKER` pin needed for a worker whose harness rotated sessions.
It explicitly warns not to mint a new id and strand the live claim.

Patch is not defensible: both changes alter caller-visible diagnostic/recovery behavior on a 0.x tool.
No Protocol.fs wire-surface change is included.

PREVIOUS RELEASE NOTES (0.16.0):

EIGHT merged engine commits since 0.15.0 across 32 source/project files. The #1900 squash commit
consolidates four reviewed input commits, making eleven pre-merge inputs in total. Protocol.fs moved,
so the generated worker contract and the published engine were out of step until this release.

FOLLOW-UP QUEUES AND THE DONE BOUNDARY (.github#1900/#1952): `followup audit` now observes every local
queue, previews reconciliation, and applies safe removal only after a durable GitHub disposition is
verified. `done` audits residual promises before stamping completion. `--apply` is now valid for the
followup command, and the JSON/text result vocabulary gains the audit and reconciliation outcomes.

FAIL-CLOSED MARKER SCANS (.github#1896/#1949): scheduler selection, claim/adopt/reap checks, and active
touch-set decisions no longer continue from a partial comment scan. A previously successful operation
may now refuse with an incomplete/undetermined result rather than silently ignoring a hidden claim.

SCHEDULING AND RANKING: BLOCKER-CLEARED respects an in-flight implementation (.github#1738/#1921);
decision items stay out of the worker queue (.github#1887/#1946); Severity is an ordered rank axis
(.github#1901); and `lint` names consolidation candidates when overlapping work is one cause
(.github#1915).

SKILL AND KIT DIAGNOSTICS: skill views are derived from receiver declarations (.github#1948), and KIT
DIGEST gives correct claim advice for skill files (.github#1942).

KNOWN RESIDUE: .github#1892 still decides whether secondary rate limits receive a distinct exit code or
remain EX_RATE with richer data. .github#1857 still tracks a session id rotating mid-item and stranding
the worker's own heartbeat/release/done operations. Neither behavior is claimed fixed by this release.
